    95	    --timeout) [[ "${2:-}" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]{0,4}$ ]] || usage "--timeout needs seconds (1-99999)"; TIMEOUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    96	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    97	    --) shift; break ;;
    98	    -h|--help) sed -n '3,41p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    99	    *) usage "unknown argument '$1' (the test command goes after --)" ;;
   100	  esac
   101	done
   102	[[ -n "$RED" ]] || usage "--red is required"
   103	[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || usage "a test command is required after --"
   104	case "$RED" in -*) usage "--red must be a commit, not an option" ;; esac
   105	case "$GREEN" in -*) usage "--green must be a revision, not an option" ;; esac
   106	case "$TEST_FILE" in
   107	  /*) usage "--test-file must be relative to the repository root" ;;
   108	  -*) usage "--test-file must be a path, not an option" ;;
   109	esac
   110	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]] && ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then die2 "--json needs jq"; fi
   111	SETUP_ARGV=()
   112	if [[ -n "$SETUP" ]]; then
   113	  read -r -a SETUP_ARGV <<< "$SETUP"
   114	  [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]] || usage "--setup is empty"
   115	fi
   116	
   117	MAIN="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree"
   118	MAIN="$(cd "$MAIN" && pwd -P)"
   119	
   120	RED_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${RED}^{commit}")" || die2 "--red '${RED}' does not resolve to a commit"
   121	GREEN_SHA="$(git -C "$MAIN" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${GREEN}^{commit}")" || die2 "--green '${GREEN}' does not resolve to a commit"
   122	if [[ "$RED_SHA" == "$GREEN_SHA" ]] || ! git -C "$MAIN" merge-base --is-ancestor "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA"; then
   123	  die2 "red ${RED_SHA} is not a strict ancestor of green ${GREEN_SHA}: commit the failing test first, then the fix"
   124	fi
   125	
   126	RED_EXIT=""
   127	GREEN_EXIT=""
   128	RED_TAIL=""
   129	GREEN_TAIL=""
   130	LINKED=""
   131	
   132	# Report a verdict (text or JSON) and exit with its code.
   133	finish(){
   134	  local verdict="$1" code="$2"
   135	  if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   136	    jq -n --arg red "$RED_SHA" --arg green "$GREEN_SHA" --arg re "$RED_EXIT" --arg ge "$GREEN_EXIT" \
   137	      --arg verdict "$verdict" --arg rt "$RED_TAIL" --arg gt "$GREEN_TAIL" --arg linked "$LINKED" \
   138	      '{red: $red, green: $green,
   139	        red_exit: (if $re == "" then null else ($re | tonumber) end),
   140	        green_exit: (if $ge == "" then null else ($ge | tonumber) end),
   141	        verdict: $verdict, red_tail: $rt, green_tail: $gt,
   142	        linked_deps: ($linked | split(" ") | map(select(. != "")))}'
   143	    if [[ -n "$RED_TAIL" ]]; then
   144	      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL" >&2
   145	    fi
   146	  else
   147	    echo "${PROG}: red ${RED_SHA} exit ${RED_EXIT:-n/a}; green ${GREEN_SHA} exit ${GREEN_EXIT:-n/a}; linked deps: ${LINKED:-none}"
   148	    if [[ -n "$RED_EXIT" ]]; then
   149	      printf -- '--- red run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end red run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$RED_TAIL"
   150	    fi
   151	    if [[ -n "$GREEN_EXIT" && "$GREEN_EXIT" != "0" ]]; then
   152	      printf -- '--- green run (last %s lines) ---\n%s\n--- end green run ---\n' "$TAIL_LINES" "$GREEN_TAIL"
   153	    fi
   154	    echo "verdict: ${verdict}"
   155	  fi
   156	  exit "$code"
   157	}
   158	
   159	# D-7.6: the named test file must exist at the red commit.
   160	if [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" ]] && ! git -C "$MAIN" cat-file -e "${RED_SHA}:${TEST_FILE#./}" 2>/dev/null; then
   161	  echo "${PROG}: --test-file '${TEST_FILE}' does not exist at the red commit ${RED_SHA}: the failing test was not committed there" >&2
   162	  finish NOT_A_RED 4
   163	fi
   164	
   165	# WARN: a green that differs from red only in test files cannot be a fix.
   166	is_test_path(){
   167	  local p="$1" b
   168	  b="${p##*/}"
   169	  [[ -n "$TEST_FILE" && "$p" == "${TEST_FILE#./}" ]] && return 0
   170	  case "/$p" in */test/*|*/tests/*|*/spec/*|*/__tests__/*|*/testdata/*|*/fixtures/*) return 0 ;; esac
   171	  case "$b" in test_*|*_test.*|*.test.*|*.spec.*|*_spec.*|*.bats) return 0 ;; esac
   172	  return 1
   173	}
   174	nontest=0
   175	while IFS= read -r p; do
   176	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   177	  if ! is_test_path "$p"; then nontest=1; break; fi
   178	done < <(git -C "$MAIN" diff --name-only "$RED_SHA" "$GREEN_SHA" -- 2>/dev/null || true)
   179	if [[ "$nontest" -eq 0 ]]; then
   180	  echo "${PROG}: WARN: no non-test file changed between red ${RED_SHA} and green ${GREEN_SHA}; a pass there comes from test changes alone" >&2
   181	fi
   182	
   183	SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/red-test-check.XXXXXX")"
   184	SCRATCH="$(cd "$SCRATCH" && pwd -P)"
   185	WT_RED=""
   186	WT_GREEN=""
   187	RUN_PID=""
   188	WATCH_PID=""
   189	remove_wt(){
   190	  local wt="$1" d
   191	  [[ -n "$wt" ]] || return 0
   192	  # Unlink our dependency symlinks first, so nothing below can follow them into the live tree.
   193	  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
   194	    if [[ -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then rm -f -- "${wt}/${d}"; fi
   195	  done
   196	  git -C "$MAIN" worktree remove --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   197	}
   198	cleanup(){
   199	  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
   200	  if [[ -n "$RUN_PID" ]]; then
   201	    kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   202	  fi
   203	  remove_wt "$WT_RED"
   204	  remove_wt "$WT_GREEN"
   205	  git -C "$MAIN" worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   206	  if [[ -n "$SCRATCH" && -d "$SCRATCH" ]]; then rm -rf -- "$SCRATCH"; fi
   207	  return 0
   208	}
   209	trap cleanup EXIT
   210	trap 'exit 130' INT
   211	trap 'exit 143' TERM
   212	
   213	add_wt(){
   214	  local path="$1" sha="$2"
   215	  # No hook from the shared hooks directory runs for our checkout.
   216	  if ! git -C "$MAIN" -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null worktree add --detach "$path" "$sha" >/dev/null 2>"${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err"; then
   217	    strip < "${SCRATCH}/wt-add.err" >&2
   218	    die2 "could not create a worktree for ${sha}; nothing ran"
   219	  fi
   220	}
   221	
   222	link_deps(){
   223	  local wt="$1" d
   224	  [[ "$LINK_DEPS" -eq 1 ]] || return 0
   225	  for d in $DEP_DIRS; do
   226	    if [[ -e "${MAIN}/${d}" && ! -e "${wt}/${d}" && ! -L "${wt}/${d}" ]]; then
   227	      ln -s "${MAIN}/${d}" "${wt}/${d}"
   228	      case " $LINKED " in *" $d "*) ;; *) LINKED="${LINKED:+$LINKED }$d" ;; esac
   229	    fi
   230	  done
   231	}
   232	
   233	# Run argv with cwd $1, output to $2, bounded by TIMEOUT. Sets RUN_RC and RUN_TIMED_OUT.
   234	RUN_RC=0
   235	RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
   236	run_bounded(){
   237	  local cwd="$1" log="$2" flag="${SCRATCH}/timed-out" tbin="" start
   238	  shift 2
   239	  rm -f -- "$flag"
   240	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=timeout
   241	  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then tbin=gtimeout
   242	  fi
   243	  start=$SECONDS
   244	  # Job control gives the run its own process group, so a timeout or an interrupt stops the
   245	  # whole tree it spawned.
   246	  set -m
   247	  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
   248	    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$tbin" -k 2 "$TIMEOUT" "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   249	  else
   250	    ( cd "$cwd" && unset GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX && exec "$@" ) > "$log" 2>&1 < /dev/null &
   251	  fi
   252	  RUN_PID=$!
   253	  set +m
   254	  if [[ -z "$tbin" ]]; then
   255	    ( i=0
   256	      while kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
   257	        if [[ "$i" -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; then
   258	          : > "$flag"
   259	          kill -TERM -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   260	          sleep 2
   261	          kill -KILL -- "-${RUN_PID}" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   262	          exit 0
   263	        fi
   264	        sleep 1
   265	        i=$((i + 1))
   266	      done ) < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   267	    WATCH_PID=$!
   268	  fi
   269	  set +e
   270	  wait "$RUN_PID"
   271	  RUN_RC=$?
   272	  set -e
   273	  RUN_PID=""
   274	  if [[ -n "$WATCH_PID" ]]; then
   275	    kill "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   276	    wait "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
   277	    WATCH_PID=""
   278	  fi
   279	  RUN_TIMED_OUT=0
   280	  if [[ -n "$tbin" ]]; then
   281	    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 124 ]] || { [[ "$RUN_RC" -eq 137 ]] && [[ $((SECONDS - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]]; }; then RUN_TIMED_OUT=1; fi
   282	  elif [[ -f "$flag" ]]; then
   283	    RUN_TIMED_OUT=1
   284	  fi
   285	  return 0
   286	}
   287	
   288	prepare(){
   289	  local wt="$1" name="$2"
   290	  link_deps "$wt"
   291	  if [[ ${#SETUP_ARGV[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
   292	    run_bounded "$wt" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" "${SETUP_ARGV[@]}"
   293	    if [[ "$RUN_RC" -ne 0 || "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then
   294	      tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/setup-${name}.log" | strip >&2
   295	      if [[ "$RUN_TIMED_OUT" -eq 1 ]]; then die2 "--setup timed out after ${TIMEOUT}s in the ${name} worktree"; fi
   296	      die2 "--setup exited ${RUN_RC} in the ${name} worktree"
   297	    fi
   298	  fi
   299	}
   300	
   301	WT_RED="${SCRATCH}/red"
   302	add_wt "$WT_RED" "$RED_SHA"
   303	WT_GREEN="${SCRATCH}/green"
   304	add_wt "$WT_GREEN" "$GREEN_SHA"
   305	prepare "$WT_RED" red
   306	prepare "$WT_GREEN" green
   307	
   308	run_bounded "$WT_RED" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" "$@"
   309	RED_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
   310	RED_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
   311	RED_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/red.log" | strip)"
   312	
   313	run_bounded "$WT_GREEN" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" "$@"
   314	GREEN_EXIT="$RUN_RC"
   315	GREEN_TO="$RUN_TIMED_OUT"
   316	GREEN_TAIL="$(tail -n "$TAIL_LINES" "${SCRATCH}/green.log" | strip)"
   317	
   318	if [[ "$RED_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
   319	  echo "${PROG}: the red run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
   320	  finish TIMEOUT 5
   321	fi
   322	if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 0 ]]; then
   323	  echo "${PROG}: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug" >&2
   324	  finish DECOY 3
   325	fi
   326	if [[ "$RED_EXIT" -eq 126 || "$RED_EXIT" -eq 127 ]]; then
   327	  echo "${PROG}: the red run exited ${RED_EXIT} (command not found or not executable): not an assertion failure" >&2
   328	  finish NOT_A_RED 4
   329	fi
   330	# Strip once into a file: `strip | grep -q` under pipefail can turn a match into a miss.
   331	strip < "${SCRATCH}/red.log" > "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"
   332	for pat in "${NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
   333	  if grep -qE -- "$pat" "${SCRATCH}/red.clean"; then
   334	    echo "${PROG}: the red run failed by a non-assertion error (matched '${pat}'): fix the test so it loads, then re-check" >&2
   335	    finish NOT_A_RED 4
   336	  fi
   337	done
   338	if [[ "$GREEN_TO" -eq 1 ]]; then
   339	  echo "${PROG}: the green run exceeded ${TIMEOUT}s" >&2
   340	  finish TIMEOUT 5
   341	fi
   342	if [[ "$GREEN_EXIT" -ne 0 ]]; then
   343	  echo "${PROG}: the test still fails at green ${GREEN_SHA}" >&2
   344	  finish GREEN_FAILS 1
   345	fi
   346	finish VERIFIED 0

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh: does every backticked framework term in the
     4	# kernel resolve to a glossary entry?
     5	#
     6	# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
     7	# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
     8	# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
     9	# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
    10	# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
    11	# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
    12	# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
    13	# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
    14	# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
    15	# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
    16	#
    17	# Usage:
    18	#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
    19	#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
    20	#
    21	#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
    22	#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
    23	#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
    24	#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
    25	#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
    26	#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
    27	#
    28	# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
    29	#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
    30	#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    36	
    37	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    38	KERNEL="$ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    39	GLOSSARY="$ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    40	ALLOWLIST="$ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
    41	ALLOWLIST_MAX=30
    42	JSON=0
    43	REPORT=0
    44	ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"
    45	
    46	need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }
    47	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    51	    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
    53	    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    56	  esac
    57	done
    58	
    59	for f in "$KERNEL" "$GLOSSARY" "$ALLOWLIST"; do
    60	  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "$ME: cannot read $f" >&2; exit 2; }
    61	done
    62	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
    63	  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "$ME: --json needs jq" >&2; exit 2; }
    64	fi
    65	
    66	# Display names: repo-relative when the file sits under the repo root.
    67	rel() { case "$1" in "$ROOT"/*) printf '%s' "${1#"$ROOT"/}" ;; *) printf '%s' "$1" ;; esac; }
    68	DK="$(rel "$KERNEL")"; DG="$(rel "$GLOSSARY")"; DA="$(rel "$ALLOWLIST")"
    69	
    70	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-glossary-terms.XXXXXX")"
    71	trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
    72	
    73	# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.
    74	awk '
    75	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    76	  fence { next }
    77	  {
    78	    s = $0
    79	    while (match(s, /`[^`]+`/)) {
    80	      t = substr(s, RSTART + 1, RLENGTH - 2)
    81	      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)
    82	      if (t ~ /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ && !(t in seen)) { seen[t] = 1; printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, t }
    83	    }
    84	  }
    85	' "$KERNEL" > "$WORK/tokens.tsv"
    86	
    87	# 2. Glossary names, "kind<TAB>name<TAB>entry": kind is term or alias, entry is
    88	#    the **Term** the name belongs to. Only the "## Language" section counts.
    89	awk '
    90	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }
    91	  fence { next }
    92	  /^## / { h = $0; sub(/^## +/, "", h); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", h); lang = (h == "Language"); next }
    93	  /^# / { lang = 0; next }
    94	  !lang { next }
    95	  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
    96	    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
    97	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
    98	    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
    99	  }
   100	  /^_Aliases_:/ {
   101	    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
   102	    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)
   105	      if (p != "") printf "alias\t%s\t%s\n", p, entry
   106	    }
   107	  }
   108	' "$GLOSSARY" > "$WORK/names.tsv"
   109	
   110	# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).
   111	awk '
   112	  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)
   113	    if (s == "") next
   114	    split(s, f, /[[:space:]]+/); printf "%d\t%s\n", NR, f[1] }
   115	' "$ALLOWLIST" > "$WORK/allow.tsv"
   116	
   117	# 4. Resolve. "resolution<TAB>token<TAB>line<TAB>entry" for each kept token
   118	#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
   119	#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no
   120	#    longer occur in the kernel and "REDUNDANT<TAB>…<TAB>entry" for ones the
   121	#    glossary already resolves.
   122	awk -F'\t' '
   123	  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
   124	  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
   125	  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
   126	  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
   127	  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)
   128	                            if (x ~ /es$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 2), v)
   129	                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }
   130	  function lookup(map, x,   k) { k = norm(x); return (k in map) ? map[k] : "" }
   131	  FILENAME == ARGV[1] { if ($1 == "term") add(term, $2, $3); else add(alias, $2, $3); next }
   132	  FILENAME == ARGV[2] { allow[norm($2)] = $1; allowtok[norm($2)] = $2; next }
   133	  {
   134	    used[norm($2)] = 1
   135	    if ((e = lookup(term, $2)) != "") r = "defined"
   136	    else if ((e = lookup(alias, $2)) != "") r = "alias"
   137	    else if (norm($2) in allow) { r = "allowlisted"; e = "" }
   138	    else { r = "MISS"; e = "" }
   139	    printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", r, $2, $1, e
   140	  }
   141	  END {
   142	    for (k in allow) {
   143	      if (!(k in used)) printf "STALE\t%s\t%s\t\n", allowtok[k], allow[k]
   144	      else if ((e = lookup(term, allowtok[k])) != "" || (e = lookup(alias, allowtok[k])) != "")
   145	        printf "REDUNDANT\t%s\t%s\t%s\n", allowtok[k], allow[k], e
   146	    }
   147	  }
   148	' "$WORK/names.tsv" "$WORK/allow.tsv" "$WORK/tokens.tsv" > "$WORK/resolved.tsv"
   149	
   150	kept="$(wc -l < "$WORK/tokens.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   151	allow_count="$(wc -l < "$WORK/allow.tsv" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   152	n_of() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" '$1 == k' "$WORK/resolved.tsv" | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
   153	n_def="$(n_of defined)"; n_alias="$(n_of alias)"; n_allow="$(n_of allowlisted)"; n_miss="$(n_of MISS)"
   154	
   155	violations=()
   156	warnings=()
   157	while IFS=$'\t' read -r r tok ln entry; do
   158	  case "$r" in

     6	# The kernel (.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md) is the only extraction scope. Every
     7	# backticked span outside fenced code is a candidate; a span is kept only when
     8	# it matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, which drops paths, scripts, flags,
     9	# commands and config keys (anything with "/", ".", "--", ":" or "(") as well
    10	# as spaced phrases and operators. A kept token resolves when it matches,
    11	# case-insensitively, a **Term** entry or an _Aliases_: token in the glossary's
    12	# "## Language" section, with a plural "s" or "es" folded and "-", "_" and a
    13	# space treated alike; or when the allowlist names it. The allowlist holds
    14	# code identifiers the heuristic cannot tell from a term: one token per line,
    15	# "#" starts a comment (give the reason there), at most 30 entries.
    16	#

    18	#   tools/check-glossary-terms.sh [--kernel PATH] [--glossary PATH]
    19	#                                 [--allowlist PATH] [--json] [--report]
    20	#
    21	#   --kernel PATH     default .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md
    22	#   --glossary PATH   default .claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md
    23	#   --allowlist PATH  default .claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt
    24	#   --json            one JSON report on stdout
    25	#   --report          list every kept token with its resolution
    26	#                     (defined, alias, allowlisted or MISS)
    27	#
    28	# Exit codes: 0 every token resolves (a stale allowlist entry only WARNs)
    29	#             1 a token misses, or the allowlist has more than 30 entries
    30	#             2 usage, or an input file is unreadable
    31	# =============================================================================
    32	set -euo pipefail
    33	export LC_ALL=C
    34	
    35	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }

    37	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

    42	JSON=0
    43	REPORT=0
    44	ME="check-glossary-terms.sh"

    46	need_arg() { [[ $2 -ge 2 ]] || { echo "$ME: $1 needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }; }

    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --kernel)    need_arg "$1" $#; KERNEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --glossary)  need_arg "$1" $#; GLOSSARY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    51	    --allowlist) need_arg "$1" $#; ALLOWLIST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    52	    --json)   JSON=1; shift ;;
    53	    --report) REPORT=1; shift ;;
    54	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    55	    *) echo "$ME: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    56	  esac
    57	done

    64	fi

    73	# 1. Kept kernel tokens, "line<TAB>token", first occurrence only, in order.

    75	  /^[[:space:]]*(```|~~~)/ { fence = !fence; next }

    77	  {
    78	    s = $0

    81	      s = substr(s, RSTART + RLENGTH)

    94	  !lang { next }
    95	  /^\*\*[^*]+\*\*:/ {
    96	    t = $0; sub(/^\*\*/, "", t); sub(/\*\*:.*$/, "", t); gsub(/`/, "", t)
    97	    gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", t)
    98	    entry = t; printf "term\t%s\t%s\n", t, entry; next
    99	  }
   100	  /^_Aliases_:/ {
   101	    a = $0; sub(/^_Aliases_:[[:space:]]*/, "", a); gsub(/`/, "", a)
   102	    n = split(a, parts, /,/)
   103	    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
   104	      p = parts[i]; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", p)

   106	    }
   107	  }

   109	
   110	# 3. Allowlist entries, "line<TAB>token" (comment and blank lines dropped).

   112	  { s = $0; sub(/#.*/, "", s); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", s)

   118	#    ("MISS" with an empty entry when nothing matches), then
   119	#    "STALE<TAB>token<TAB>allowlist-line<TAB>" for allowlist entries that no

   123	  function norm(x) { x = tolower(x); gsub(/[-_ ]+/, " ", x); return x }
   124	  function put(map, k, v) { if (!(k in map)) map[k] = v }
   125	  # every spelling a name answers to: itself, its s and es plurals, and, for
   126	  # a plural name, its singular (the plural fold is applied here only)
   127	  function add(map, x, v) { x = norm(x); put(map, x, v); put(map, x "s", v); put(map, x "es", v)

   129	                            if (x ~ /s$/) put(map, substr(x, 1, length(x) - 1), v) }

   146	    }
   147	  }

     1	# Glossary: Loa framework
     2	
     3	The shared language of the Loa agent framework, for humans and agents. It is mounted into every project with the framework and defines what each word means in day-to-day work; the mythic background of the names lives in the lore, and a project's own terms belong in that project's root glossary, never here.
     4	
     5	## Language
     6	
     7	**Beads**: The local-first task tracker that is the single source of truth for sprint tasks, decision tickets and their dependencies.
     8	_Aliases_: br
     9	
    10	**Bridgebuilder**: The automated pull-request reviewer that posts findings on a pull request and drives the iterative improvement loop of a bridge run.
    11	
    12	**Cheval**: The model-dispatch substrate through which every call to an external model provider is routed, with fallback, budget limits and cost accounting.
    13	
    14	**Circuit breaker**: The run-mode guard that halts a run after repeated identical findings, no progress, a cycle limit or a timeout, leaving the run for the operator to resume.
    15	
    16	**Construct**: An installable package of skills, personas and grimoire paths that extends the framework for a domain and may declare its own workflow gates.
    17	
    18	**DEC row**: One entry of the decision ledger, numbered DEC-NNNN, recording a decision, its alternatives, its status and the voice that proposed or decided it.
    19	_Avoid_: ADR, decision note
    20	
    21	**Decision ticket**: A question-type bead under a map epic whose resolution is a decision, not a build slice.
    22	_Avoid_: question task
    23	
    24	**decision:grilling**: The label of a decision ticket that talking can settle, answered in interview rounds with the operator.
    25	
    26	**decision:prototype**: The label of a decision ticket the operator needs to see before answering, settled by a spike and its verdict.
    27	
    28	**decision:research**: The label of a decision ticket that needs reading or sources, answered by a read-only research report and one confirming round.
    29	
    30	**decision:unblock**: The label of a decision ticket that a read-only probe settles by showing whether a suspected blocker is real; it never builds anything.
    31	
    32	**Dissent**: A second model's independent review of the same diff, triaged before a gate verdict.
    33	_Avoid_: second opinion, cross-check
    34	
    35	**Flatline**: The multi-model adversarial review of planning documents, in which independent voices review and cross-score each other before findings are integrated.
    36	_Aliases_: Flatline Protocol
    37	
    38	**Fog of war**: Decisions an effort can tell are coming but cannot yet phrase sharply; a map keeps them under Not yet specified.
    39	
    40	**Frontier**: The open, unblocked, unclaimed decision tickets of a map; in an interview, the questions whose prerequisites are already settled.
    41	
    42	**Golden path**: The five everyday commands (loa, plan, build, review and ship) that detect where the workflow stands and route to the right truename.
    43	
    44	**Grimoire**: The project's state area of planning documents, notes, reviews and records that agents read and write across sessions.
    45	
    46	**ICE**: Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics, the git safety layer of run mode that owns branch creation, push decisions and the refusal to touch protected branches.
    47	
    48	**Implement gate**: The hook that asks before an edit to application code made outside the implement or bug workflows.
    49	
    50	**Jack in**: To start an autonomous run under run mode; a run that has finished or been stopped for good has jacked out.
    51	_Aliases_: jack out
    52	
    53	**Kaironic**: Stopping at the right moment rather than after a fixed count: an iterative review loop ends when successive passes stop finding material issues.
    54	_Avoid_: converged
    55	
    56	**Karpathy principles**: The four working rules applied on every code-touching turn: think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes and goal-driven verification.
    57	
    58	**Known failure**: A recorded degradation with its symptom, the attempts made and a reading guide, consulted before triage so that prior dead ends are not retried.
    59	_Aliases_: KF
    60	
    61	**Lore**: The mythic and narrative background of the framework's names, kept apart from this glossary, which defines only working meanings.
    62	
    63	**Map epic**: The epic bead that parents an effort's decision tickets, paired with a map document of its destination, decisions so far, fog and exclusions; run mode never implements it.
    64	
    65	**Round**: One frontier of interview questions asked together and answered together.
    66	
    67	**Run mode**: Unattended execution of a sprint plan with a circuit breaker, wrapping implement, review and audit in a loop. Its states are running, halted and jacked out.
    68	_Aliases_: RUNNING, HALTED, JACKED_OUT
    69	
    70	**Seam**: A point where a test observes the system, declared in a sprint plan together with what it catches, what it misses and its prior art.
    71	
    72	**Spike**: A throwaway prototype on its own branch that answers one decision ticket; only its report and its verdict row reach the working branch.
    73	
    74	**Truename**: The underlying command that a golden-path command routes to, used directly by power users.
    75	
    76	**Verdict trailer**: The machine-readable last line of a review or audit feedback document, which must agree with its findings. Any critical or high finding forces a changes-required verdict.
    77	_Aliases_: LOA-VERDICT
    78	
    79	**Voice**: The party a decision or finding is attributed to: the operator, the agent, Flatline or dissent.
    80	
    81	**Zone**: One of the three permission regions of a repository: the System zone holds the framework and is never edited by hand, the State zone is read and written freely, and the App zone needs confirmation before a write.
====PROJ
     1	# Glossary: Loa
     2	
     3	The terms people working on the Loa repository itself use, beyond the framework vocabulary in the framework glossary that ships with Loa. In other projects this file is the project glossary: the planning skills create it lazily at the project root the first time a term needs pinning, and update it inline.
     4	
     5	## Language
     6	
     7	**Cycle**: One numbered development iteration of the framework, from its requirements document through its sprints to the merged pull request and the archived records.
     8	
     9	**Record branch**: A pushed branch that preserves a cycle's untracked review and audit records after the cycle merges, so the evidence outlives the working tree.
    10	
    11	**Zone marker**: The temporary authorization a cycle creates at its start so that its own sprints may change the System zone, and deletes at its end.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# .claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-7.5..D-7.7, §5.2) against small
     3	# fixture repositories built per test. Every case also asserts that `git worktree list` in the
     4	# fixture shows only the main tree afterwards and that the live tree was not touched.
     5	
     6	setup() {
     7	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
     8	    SCRIPT="${PROJECT_ROOT}/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh"
     9	    R="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/repo"
    10	    export TMPDIR="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/tmp"
    11	    mkdir -p "$R" "$TMPDIR"
    12	    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    13	    git -C "$R" init -q
    14	    git -C "$R" config user.email t@example.invalid
    15	    git -C "$R" config user.name t
    16	    git -C "$R" config commit.gpgsign false
    17	    # Base: a buggy add(); node_modules is ignored, as in a real project.
    18	    printf 'node_modules/\n.venv/\n' > "$R/.gitignore"
    19	    printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 - $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"
    20	    commit "base"
    21	}
    22	
    23	commit() { git -C "$R" add -A && git -C "$R" commit -q -m "$1"; git -C "$R" rev-parse HEAD; }
    24	
    25	# The red test: asserts add 2 3 = 5 and prints what it got.
    26	add_red_test() {
    27	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
    28	    cat > "$R/tests/test_add.sh" <<'EOF'
    29	. ./lib.sh
    30	got="$(add 2 3)"
    31	if [ "$got" = 5 ]; then echo "PASS add"; exit 0; fi
    32	echo "FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got $got"
    33	exit 1
    34	EOF
    35	}
    36	fix_lib() { printf 'add() { echo $(( $1 + $2 )); }\n' > "$R/lib.sh"; }
    37	
    38	# Status of the fixture after a run: only the main tree, no stash, the live tree as it was.
    39	assert_clean() {
    40	    local n
    41	    n="$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    42	    [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || { git -C "$R" worktree list; echo "worktrees left behind"; return 1; }
    43	    [ -z "$(git -C "$R" stash list)" ] || { echo "a stash was created"; return 1; }
    44	    [ -z "$(ls -A "$TMPDIR")" ] || { ls -la "$TMPDIR"; echo "scratch left behind"; return 1; }
    45	}
    46	
    47	rtc() { (cd "$R" && "$SCRIPT" "$@"); }
    48	
    49	@test "RTC-1 red fails by assertion, green passes: exit 0 VERIFIED with the red output printed" {
    50	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
    51	    fix_lib; commit "fix(bug): add adds" >/dev/null
    52	    run rtc --red "$red" --test-file tests/test_add.sh -- sh tests/test_add.sh
    53	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
    54	    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: VERIFIED"* ]]
    55	    [[ "$output" == *"--- red run (last 80 lines) ---"*"FAIL: add 2 3: expected 5, got -1"*"--- end red run ---"* ]]
    56	    [[ "$output" != *"WARN: no non-test file changed"* ]]
    57	    assert_clean
    58	}

    76	    [[ "$output" == *"does not exist at the red commit"* ]]

   104	    assert_clean

   107	@test "RTC-6 a pytest-style collection error in the red output is NOT_A_RED, exit 4" {
   108	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
   109	    printf 'echo "ERROR collecting tests/test_add.py"\necho "ImportError while importing test module"\nexit 2\n' > "$R/tests/test_collect.sh"
   110	    red="$(commit "test: does not collect")"
   111	    fix_lib; printf 'exit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_collect.sh"; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   112	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_collect.sh
   113	    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   114	    [[ "$output" == *"matched 'ERROR collecting'"* ]]
   115	    assert_clean
   116	}
   117	
   118	@test "RTC-7 a green that still fails exits 1 GREEN_FAILS and prints the green output" {
   119	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
   120	    printf 'notes\n' > "$R/NOTES"; commit "not a fix" >/dev/null
   121	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   122	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   123	    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: GREEN_FAILS"* ]]
   124	    [[ "$output" == *"--- green run (last 80 lines) ---"* ]]
   125	    assert_clean
   126	}

   128	@test "RTC-8 a run past --timeout yields TIMEOUT, exit 5, and stops the run's children" {
   129	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'sleep 30 &\nwait\n' > "$R/tests/test_slow.sh"
   130	    red="$(commit "test: slow")"
   131	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   132	    local start=$SECONDS
   133	    run rtc --red "$red" --timeout 1 -- sh tests/test_slow.sh
   134	    [ "$status" -eq 5 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   135	    [[ "$output" == *"TIMEOUT"* ]]
   136	    [ $((SECONDS - start)) -lt 20 ]
   137	    assert_clean
   138	}
   139	
   140	@test "RTC-9 without timeout/gtimeout on PATH the bash watcher yields TIMEOUT, exit 5" {
   141	    local shim="${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/shim" f b
   142	    mkdir -p "$shim"
   143	    for f in /usr/local/bin/* /usr/bin/* /bin/*; do
   144	        b="${f##*/}"
   145	        case "$b" in timeout|gtimeout) continue ;; esac
   146	        [ -e "$shim/$b" ] || ln -s "$f" "$shim/$b" 2>/dev/null || true
   147	    done
   148	    PATH="$shim" command -v timeout && { echo "the shim still exposes timeout"; return 1; }
   149	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'sleep 30\n' > "$R/tests/test_slow.sh"
   150	    red="$(commit "test: slow")"
   151	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   152	    local start=$SECONDS
   153	    run env PATH="$shim" bash -c 'cd "$1" && shift && exec "$@"' _ "$R" "$SCRIPT" --red "$red" --timeout 1 -- sh tests/test_slow.sh
   154	    [ "$status" -eq 5 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   155	    [[ "$output" == *"verdict: TIMEOUT"* ]]
   156	    [ $((SECONDS - start)) -lt 20 ]
   157	    assert_clean
   158	}

   160	@test "RTC-10 a dependency present only in the live tree is linked by default; --no-link-deps makes it NOT_A_RED" {
   161	    mkdir -p "$R/node_modules/dep" "$R/tests"
   162	    printf 'dep_ok() { echo yes; }\n' > "$R/node_modules/dep/index.sh"
   163	    cat > "$R/tests/test_dep.sh" <<'EOF'
   164	[ -f node_modules/dep/index.sh ] || { echo "Error: Cannot find module 'dep'"; exit 1; }
   165	. ./node_modules/dep/index.sh
   166	. ./lib.sh
   167	[ "$(dep_ok)" = yes ] && [ "$(add 2 3)" = 5 ] && { echo "PASS"; exit 0; }
   168	echo "FAIL: add 2 3 = $(add 2 3)"; exit 1
   169	EOF
   170	    red="$(commit "test(bug): needs dep")"
   171	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   172	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_dep.sh
   173	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   174	    [[ "$output" == *"linked deps: node_modules"* ]]
   175	    assert_clean
   176	    # the live tree's dependency survived the cleanup
   177	    [ -f "$R/node_modules/dep/index.sh" ]
   178	    run rtc --red "$red" --no-link-deps -- sh tests/test_dep.sh
   179	    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   180	    [[ "$output" == *"Cannot find module"* ]]
   181	    assert_clean
   182	}
   183	
   184	@test "RTC-11 --setup runs in both worktrees before the test; a failing --setup exits 2" {
   185	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"
   186	    cat > "$R/tests/test_setup.sh" <<'EOF'
   187	[ -f .setup-ran ] || { echo "ImportError while importing: setup did not run"; exit 1; }
   188	. ./lib.sh
   189	[ "$(add 2 3)" = 5 ] && exit 0
   190	echo "FAIL: add"; exit 1
   191	EOF
   192	    red="$(commit "test(bug): needs setup")"
   193	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   194	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_setup.sh
   195	    [ "$status" -eq 4 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   196	    assert_clean
   197	    run rtc --red "$red" --setup "touch .setup-ran" -- sh tests/test_setup.sh
   198	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   199	    [ ! -e "$R/.setup-ran" ]
   200	    assert_clean
   201	    run rtc --red "$red" --setup "false" -- sh tests/test_setup.sh
   202	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   203	    [[ "$output" == *"--setup exited 1"* ]]
   204	    assert_clean
   205	}

   207	@test "RTC-12 red not a strict ancestor of green, or unresolvable, exits 2 and creates nothing" {
   208	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test")"
   209	    fix_lib; green="$(commit "fix")"
   210	    run rtc --red "$green" --green "$red" -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   211	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; [[ "$output" == *"not a strict ancestor"* ]]
   212	    run rtc --red "$green" -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   213	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   214	    run rtc --red deadbeefdeadbeef -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   215	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; [[ "$output" == *"does not resolve"* ]]
   216	    run rtc --red "$red"
   217	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]; [[ "$output" == *"a test command is required"* ]]
   218	    run rtc --red --upload-pack=x -- true
   219	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   220	    assert_clean
   221	}
   222	
   223	@test "RTC-13 --json prints the documented object" {
   224	    command -v jq >/dev/null || skip "jq not installed"
   225	    mkdir -p "$R/node_modules"
   226	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
   227	    fix_lib; green="$(commit "fix")"
   228	    run bash -c 'cd "$1" && "$2" --red "$3" --json -- sh tests/test_add.sh 2>/dev/null' _ "$R" "$SCRIPT" "$red"
   229	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   230	    jq -e --arg r "$red" --arg g "$green" '
   231	        (keys == ["green","green_exit","green_tail","linked_deps","red","red_exit","red_tail","verdict"])
   232	        and .red == $r and .green == $g and .red_exit == 1 and .green_exit == 0
   233	        and .verdict == "VERIFIED" and (.red_tail | test("expected 5, got -1"))
   234	        and (.green_tail | test("PASS add")) and .linked_deps == ["node_modules"]' <<< "$output"
   235	    assert_clean
   236	}

   239	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
   240	    printf 'echo "PASS rewritten"\nexit 0\n' > "$R/tests/test_add.sh"; commit "weaken the test" >/dev/null
   241	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   242	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   243	    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: no non-test file changed"* ]]
   244	    assert_clean
   245	}

   247	@test "RTC-15 uncommitted live edits never count, and the live tree is left as it was" {
   248	    add_red_test; red="$(commit "test(bug): failing test")"
   249	    printf 'notes\n' > "$R/NOTES"; commit "not a fix" >/dev/null
   250	    fix_lib    # the fix exists only as an uncommitted edit
   251	    local before; before="$(git -C "$R" status --porcelain)"
   252	    run rtc --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_add.sh
   253	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
   254	    [ "$(git -C "$R" status --porcelain)" = "$before" ]
   255	    grep -q '+ \$2' "$R/lib.sh"
   256	    assert_clean
   257	}
   258	
   259	@test "RTC-16 an interrupted run (TERM) still removes both worktrees" {
   260	    mkdir -p "$R/tests"; printf 'sleep 30\n' > "$R/tests/test_slow.sh"
   261	    red="$(commit "test: slow")"
   262	    fix_lib; commit "fix" >/dev/null
   263	    (cd "$R" && exec "$SCRIPT" --red "$red" -- sh tests/test_slow.sh) > "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/int.out" 2>&1 &
   264	    local pid=$! i=0
   265	    while [ "$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -lt 3 ] && [ "$i" -lt 100 ]; do sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1)); done
   266	    [ "$(git -C "$R" worktree list | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -eq 3 ]
   267	    sleep 0.5
   268	    kill -TERM "$pid"
   269	    local rc=0; wait "$pid" || rc=$?
   270	    [ "$rc" -eq 143 ] || { cat "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR}/int.out"; echo "rc=$rc"; return 1; }
   271	    assert_clean
   272	}

   274	@test "RTC-17 the micro-sprint template requires the separate red commit; reviewing-code names the script" {
   275	    local m="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md"
   276	    local t1; t1="$(awk '/^#### Task 1:/,/^#### Task 2:/' "$m")"
   277	    grep -qF 'Committed alone (`test(<bug_id>): failing test`) before any fix commit' <<< "$t1"
   278	    grep -qF 'Red commit: <sha>' <<< "$t1"
   279	    awk '/^#### Task 2:/,/^### Acceptance Criteria/' "$m" | grep -qF 'The fix is a later commit and does not weaken the test'
   280	    local r="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md"
   281	    awk '/^## Phase 2: Code Review/,/^## Phase 2.5/' "$r" | grep -qF '.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit from reviewer.md> -- <test command>'
   282	    awk '/^## Phase 2: Code Review/,/^## Phase 2.5/' "$r" | grep -qF 'Tests exist at each declared `### Seams Under Test` seam'
   283	    grep -qF 'Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)' "$r"
   284	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/glossary-terms.bats
     4	#
     5	# tools/check-glossary-terms.sh (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-6.2, §5.3) keeps every
     6	# backticked span of the kernel that matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ outside
     7	# fenced code and fails unless each one resolves to a glossary **Term**, an
     8	# _Aliases_: token (case-insensitive, plural s/es folded) or an allowlist line
     9	# (at most 30). Every case below works on temp copies; the live kernel,
    10	# glossary and allowlist are only ever read.
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    15	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    16	    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-glossary-terms.sh"
    17	    KERNEL="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
    18	    GLOSSARY="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/loa/GLOSSARY.md"
    19	    ALLOW="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/data/glossary-allowlist.txt"
    20	    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/glossary"
    21	    W="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    22	    printf '# Glossary: t\nTest vocabulary.\n\n## Language\n\n**Widget**: A thing.\n\n**Run mode**: Unattended runs.\n_Aliases_: RUNNING, JACKED_OUT\n\n**Box**: A container.\n' > "$W/g.md"
    23	    printf '# test allowlist\nparse_it   # code identifier\n' > "$W/a.txt"
    24	}
    25	
    26	# check <kernel text>: run the checker on a temp kernel with the temp glossary and allowlist
    27	check() {
    28	    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$W/k.md"
    29	    shift
    30	    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$W/k.md" --glossary "$W/g.md" --allowlist "$W/a.txt" "$@"
    31	}
    32	
    33	@test "GT-1 the live kernel, framework glossary and allowlist pass" {
    34	    run "$CHECK"
    35	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    36	    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 0"* ]]
    37	    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
    38	    [[ "$output" != *"WARN"* ]]
    39	}
    40	
    41	@test "GT-2 removing a term from a copy of the glossary fails and names the token" {
    42	    grep -v '^_Aliases_: br$' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
    43	    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
    44	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    45	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `br`'* ]]
    46	    [[ "$output" == *"define **br**"* ]]
    47	    [[ "$output" == *"_Aliases_: line"* ]]
    48	    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist it in"* ]]
    49	}
    50	
    51	@test "GT-3 removing the run mode entry from a copy fails on each of its aliases" {
    52	    awk '/^\*\*Run mode\*\*:/ { skip = 1; next } skip && /^_Aliases_:/ { skip = 0; next } { skip = 0; print }' "$GLOSSARY" > "$W/glossary.md"
    53	    run "$CHECK" --glossary "$W/glossary.md"
    54	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    55	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `RUNNING`'* ]]
    56	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `HALTED`'* ]]
    57	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `JACKED_OUT`'* ]]
    58	}
    59	
    60	@test "GT-4 matching is case-insensitive and folds s and es plurals" {
    61	    check 'Use a `widget`, two `Widgets`, `boxes` and `BOX`.' --report
    62	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    63	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     widget"*"-> Widget"* ]]
    64	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     Widgets"* ]]
    65	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     boxes"*"-> Box"* ]]
    66	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     BOX"* ]]
    67	}
    68	
    69	@test "GT-4b a singular token resolves to a plural term" {
    70	    printf '# Glossary: t\nctx\n\n## Language\n\n**Beads**: A tracker.\n\n**Matches**: Pairs.\n' > "$W/g.md"
    71	    check 'One `bead`, one `match`, many `BEADS`.' --report
    72	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    73	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     bead "*"-> Beads"* ]]
    74	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     match "*"-> Matches"* ]]
    75	}
    76	
    77	@test "GT-5 an _Aliases_: token resolves to its entry; a multi-word term matches with - or _" {
    78	    check 'States: `running`, `JACKED_OUT`; also `run-mode` and `run_mode`.' --report
    79	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    80	    [[ "$output" == *"alias       running"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
    81	    [[ "$output" == *"alias       JACKED_OUT"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
    82	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run-mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
    83	    [[ "$output" == *"defined     run_mode"*"-> Run mode"* ]]
    84	}
    85	
    86	@test "GT-6 an undefined token fails; a token close to a term does not resolve by accident" {
    87	    check 'A `Widgetry` and a `Sprocket`.'
    88	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    89	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Widgetry`'* ]]
    90	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Sprocket`'* ]]
    91	    [[ "$output" == *"missing: 2"* ]]
    92	}
    93	
    94	@test "GT-7 tokens inside fenced code are ignored (backtick and tilde fences)" {
    95	    check $'Prose `Widget`.\n```bash\necho `Sprocket`\n```\n~~~\n`Gizmo`\n~~~\n  ```\n  `Indented`\n  ```'
    96	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    97	    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 1;"* ]]
    98	}
    99	
   100	@test "GT-8 the shape heuristic drops paths, files, flags, keys, calls, commands, phrases and operators" {
   101	    check 'Dropped: `a/b`, `file.md`, `--flag`, `-x`, `key:value`, `call()`, `/loa`, `two words`, `>>`, `*_TEST_MODE=1`, `9lives`, `x=y`.' --report
   102	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]

   109	    [[ "$output" == *"allowlisted parse_it"* ]]
   110	    : > "$W/a.txt"
   111	    for i in $(seq 1 31); do printf 'tok%02d  # reason\n' "$i" >> "$W/a.txt"; done
   112	    check 'Call `tok01`.'
   113	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   114	    [[ "$output" == *"has 31 entries, over the limit of 30"* ]]
   115	}

   118	    : > "$W/a.txt"
   119	    for i in $(seq 1 30); do printf 'tok%02d  # reason\n' "$i" >> "$W/a.txt"; done
   120	    check 'Call `tok01`.'
   121	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   122	    [[ "$output" == *"allowlist entries: 30/30"* ]]
   123	}
   124	
   125	@test "GT-11 a stale allowlist entry WARNs and still exits 0; a redundant one WARNs too" {
   126	    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # no longer in the kernel\nwidget    # the glossary defines it\n' > "$W/a.txt"
   127	    check 'Call `parse_it` on a `Widget`.'
   128	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   129	    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: allowlist entry 'gone_fn'"*"no longer occurs"* ]]
   130	    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: allowlist entry 'widget'"*"already resolved by the glossary entry **Widget**"* ]]
   131	}
   132	
   133	@test "GT-12 --json carries the report fields" {
   134	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
   135	    printf 'parse_it  # used\ngone_fn   # stale\n' > "$W/a.txt"
   136	    check 'A `Widget`, `running`, `parse_it` and a `Sprocket`.' --json
   137	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   138	    echo "$output" | jq -e '
   139	        .ok == false and .kept == 4
   140	        and .counts == {defined: 1, alias: 1, allowlisted: 1, missing: 1}
   141	        and .missing == ["Sprocket"] and .stale_allowlist == ["gone_fn"]
   142	        and .allowlist_entries == 2 and .allowlist_max == 30
   143	        and (.tokens | map(.resolution)) == ["defined", "alias", "allowlisted", "MISS"]
   144	        and (.tokens[0] | .token == "Widget" and .line == 1 and .entry == "Widget")
   145	        and (.tokens[3].entry == null)
   146	        and (.violations | length) == 1 and (.warnings | length) == 1' >/dev/null
   147	}
   148	
   149	@test "GT-13 --json on the live files reports ok with zero misses" {
   150	    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
   151	    run "$CHECK" --json
   152	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   153	    echo "$output" | jq -e '.ok == true and .counts.missing == 0 and .kept > 0 and .allowlist_entries <= 30' >/dev/null
   154	}
   155	
   156	@test "GT-14 the miss fixture exits 1 (positive control)" {
   157	    run "$CHECK" --kernel "$FIX/miss/kernel.md" --glossary "$FIX/miss/GLOSSARY.md" --allowlist "$FIX/miss/allowlist.txt"
   158	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]

   164	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   165	    [[ "$output" == *"kernel tokens kept: 4; defined: 2; alias: 1; allowlisted: 1; missing: 0"* ]]
   166	}
   167	
   168	@test "GT-16 usage errors exit 2: unknown flag, missing path, unreadable file" {
   169	    run "$CHECK" --bogus
   170	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   171	    run "$CHECK" --kernel
   172	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]

   177	
   178	@test "GT-17 entries outside ## Language do not resolve tokens" {
   179	    printf '# Glossary: t\nctx\n\n**Widget**: Above the language section.\n\n## Language\n\n**Box**: A container.\n\n## Notes\n\n**Gizmo**: In a later section.\n' > "$W/g.md"
   180	    check 'A `Widget`, a `Box`, a `Gizmo`.'
   181	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   182	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Widget`'* ]]
   183	    [[ "$output" == *'MISS: `Gizmo`'* ]]

   186	
   187	@test "GT-18 the live allowlist stays within 30 entries and every entry carries a reason" {

content.content:
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |
====

# Security & Quality Audit Report — Sprint 1

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Scope:** The pull request in `pr/` (`pr/head.diff`, 29 files: framework and project glossaries, the kernel-term drift gate and its CI workflow, the `glossary` artifact type and the date-gated `### Seams Under Test` rule in `validate-artifact.sh`, `red-test-check.sh`, and the matching skill, template and mount-manifest edits). Citations are `head/<path>:<line>` against `pr/head/`.
**Methodology:** Systematic 5-category review (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps; Blockchain not applicable), two-voice adversarial dissent, hand reproduction in fixture repositories.

---

## Scope and prerequisites

- **Prerequisite deviation.** The review gate's `engineer-feedback.md` says CHANGES REQUIRED (trailer: 0 critical, 3 high, 5 medium, 9 low, excluded 0), not "All good". The normal Phase 0 rule stops the audit here. The task for this sprint mandates the audit run regardless, so this audit was performed against the same change and records the deviation. `adversarial-review.json` carries `metadata.model: gpt-5.5-pro`, so the review's dissent gate is COMPLETED.
- **Inputs.** `pr/PR.md` is a title line only; `reviewer.md` is that description and carries no `## AC Verification` section. The audit rests on the code in `pr/head/`, not on the report.
- **Input guardrails:** `guardrails-orchestrator.sh` returned `action: PROCEED` (injection-detection check reported `ERROR`, fail-open per the include).
- **Integrity pre-check:** `.loa.config.yaml` sets no `integrity_enforcement` key; no drift check applies.
- **Scope analysis:** `security-audit-scope.sh` ran over the workspace (193 command-exec sink files, 153 file-operation sink files repo-wide). Within the PR the sinks are `exec "$@"` and `ln -s` in `red-test-check.sh`, the awk programs in `validate-artifact.sh` and `tools/check-glossary-terms.sh`, and the `run:` steps in the workflow.
- **Workspace artefact, not a PR defect.** `pr/head/.run/audit.jsonl` is an untracked hook log written at 06:09 when the review agent wrote its feedback with cwd `pr/head`; it appears in no hunk of `pr/head.diff`.
- **Verification performed.** Built an executable overlay of `pr/head/` plus this workspace's `.claude/scripts/` under `$HOME` (`/tmp` is noexec here and the `pr/head/` copies have lost their exec bits; the diff records mode 100755). Ran all four new bats suites: 66 tests, 65 pass, 1 skip (SEAMS-8: no cycle-128 plan in this checkout), 0 fail. Reproduced findings HIGH-001, HIGH-002, HIGH-003, MED-001, MED-002, MED-004, MED-005, LOW-002, LOW-005 and LOW-007 by hand; transcripts are summarised inline.

---

## Executive Summary

The glossary and seams half of this change is sound. Both validators fail closed, the fixtures prove the kernel-term gate bites, the CI action is pinned by SHA, and the mount manifests were updated in all three lists (`head/.claude/scripts/lib/symlink-manifest.sh:79`, `head/.claude/scripts/mount-loa.sh:2147`, `head/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh:1278`). The findings there are heuristic false positives and a gate whose reach is narrower than its header claims.

`red-test-check.sh` is where the change must not merge. The script is well built in the places that are easy to get right (detached worktrees, no stash, hooks disabled on checkout, `--setup` split without a shell, cleanup on every exit path) and wrong in the three that decide its verdict. A test file that does not exist at the red commit yields VERIFIED on the prescribed invocation. Dependency directories linked from the live tree make both runs import the live tree's source, so uncommitted edits decide the verdict despite the header's promise that they never count. And the review skill's new `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)` grant turns a `deny_raw_shell` role into one that runs any argv taken from an engineer-authored file. I reproduced all three in fixture repositories, as did the review; the audit dissent's companion voice raised the third independently and added two further concerns about the same script, both confirmed.

Nothing here is CRITICAL: every path needs either a mistaken or a hostile engineer-side input, and none is reachable from outside the operator's own session. Three HIGH findings force CHANGES_REQUIRED.

**Overall Risk Level:** HIGH

**Key Statistics:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 3 |
| Medium | 7 |
| Low | 11 |

---

## Category Scores (Rubric-Based Assessment)

**Scoring Method:** Each dimension scored 1-5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md`

| Category | Score | Dimensions |
|----------|-------|------------|
| Security | 3.0/5 | IV:3 AZ:2 CI:3 IN:3 AV:4 |
| Architecture | 3.8/5 | MO:4 SC:4 RE:3 CX:4 ST:4 |
| Code Quality | 3.8/5 | RD:4 TC:4 EH:3 TS:4 DC:4 |
| DevOps | 3.8/5 | AU:4 OB:4 RC:4 AC:3 DS:4 |
| Blockchain | n/a | *(not applicable)* |
| **Overall** | **3.5/5** | *Security weighted highest* |

**Risk Level Mapping:**
- 4.5-5.0: LOW | 3.5-4.4: MODERATE | 2.5-3.4: HIGH | 1.0-2.4: CRITICAL

The weighted score lands at the MODERATE boundary; the HIGH risk level above follows the one-way rule (three confirmed HIGH findings), not the average.

**Machine-Parseable Output:** `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/2026-10-20/findings.jsonl`

---

## Changes Required

### [HIGH-001] A test file absent at the red commit yields VERIFIED

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:326` (exit-code gate), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52` (`NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS`)
**Criterion:** SEC-IV Input Validation / CQ-EH Error Handling

**Reasoning Trace:**
> The red side is accepted as an assertion failure whenever the exit is not 0, 126 or 127 and no pattern matches (`:322-337`). `sh` exits 2 with `cannot open`, `python3` exits 2 with `can't open file … No such file or directory`, `pytest` exits 4 with `file or directory not found`. None of these codes is gated and none of these strings is in the list at `:52-71`. The `--test-file` guard at `:160` would catch it, but both prescribed invocations omit the flag: `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` and `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219`.

**Description:** Reproduced in a fixture whose red commit predates the test and whose green commit adds test and fix together, which is exactly the discipline the tool exists to catch:

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <pre-test commit> -- sh tests/test_add.sh
red-test-check: red 4d165e6a… exit 2; green 52f7935d… exit 0; linked deps: none
--- red run (last 80 lines) ---
sh: 0: cannot open tests/test_add.sh: No such file
--- end red run ---
verdict: VERIFIED          (exit 0)
```

**Impact:** The reviewer is told to cite this output as the evidence for "Test fails with current code". A VERIFIED on a red commit that never contained the test is a false attestation of red-before-green, and the micro-sprint's acceptance criterion at `micro-sprint.md:43` is satisfied by exactly the commit shape it forbids.
**Remediation:** (1) Add file-not-found shapes to `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS`: `cannot open`, `No such file or directory`, `file or directory not found`, `can.t open file`, `ERROR: not found:`. (2) Treat exit 2 from `sh`/`python` and exit 4 from `pytest` as NOT_A_RED when the output names a missing path. (3) Make `--test-file` part of both prescribed invocations, or read it from the micro-sprint's `Test file:` line and refuse to run without it. (4) Add a bats case for the default path with the file absent at red, expecting exit 4 (RTC-3 covers only the `--test-file` path).
**References:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html. Review Finding 1; review dissent DISS-001. Confirmed independently by reproduction.

### [HIGH-002] Linked dependency directories make both runs resolve the live tree's source

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227` (`ln -s`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222` (`link_deps`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:27` (the header promise)
**Criterion:** SEC-CI Integrity / ARCH-RE Reliability

**Reasoning Trace:**
> `link_deps` symlinks `node_modules .venv vendor target .tox` from `$MAIN` into each worktree by default (`:47`, `:225-229`). An npm/pnpm/yarn workspace link (`node_modules/pkg -> ../src/pkg`) and an editable Python install (`.pth` naming `$MAIN/src`) both resolve relative to the real directory in the live tree, so a test in the worktree imports the live tree's code, not the checked-out commit's.

**Description:** Reproduced with a shell fixture: `node_modules/pkg -> ../src/pkg` in the live tree, a red commit holding the failing test and the buggy source, a green commit containing no fix, and the fix present only as an uncommitted edit:

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <red> -- sh tests/test_add.sh
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red d95711b6… exit 0; green 05e7686c… exit 0; linked deps: node_modules
verdict: DECOY             (exit 3; the green commit contains no fix)
```

Both runs executed the live tree's `src/pkg/lib.sh`. With the buggy source on disk instead, the same mechanism gives a VERIFIED against a green commit that contains no fix. The header at `:27` states "Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts"; the caveat at `:29-30` covers writes, not source resolution.
**Impact:** Wrong verdicts in the tool's core job for the two ecosystems the dependency list targets first. A legitimate pair is blocked as DECOY whenever the operator has the fix checked out; an uncommitted fix can mint a VERIFIED the reviewer is told to cite.
**Remediation:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with a WARN naming the directories, or refuse to link a directory that resolves back into `$MAIN`: for `.venv`/`.tox` scan `site-packages` for `*.pth` and `__editable__*` entries that reference `$MAIN`; for `node_modules` refuse when any top-level or scoped entry is a symlink resolving outside `node_modules`. Point the help text at `--setup` for per-worktree installs. Add a bats case with a workspace-style link that expects NOT_A_RED or a refusal, never DECOY. Amend `:27` to state the remaining caveat.
**References:** CWE-706 Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html. Review Finding 2; review dissent DISS-C-002. Confirmed independently by reproduction.

### [HIGH-003] The review role's allowlist now contains a universal exec wrapper

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6` (`allowed-tools`), `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:27` (`args: ["*"]`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:250` (`exec "$@"`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:113` (`--setup` argv)
**Criterion:** SEC-AZ Authorization

**Reasoning Trace:**
> The review skill declares `deny_raw_shell: true` (`:39`) and allowlists `git diff`, `git log` and a fixed set of scripts. The change adds `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)`. The script validates `--red`, `--green`, `--timeout` and `--test-file` and then execs everything after `--` verbatim (`:248`, `:250`), plus a second arbitrary argv from `--setup` (`:113`, `:292`). Phase 2 at `SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to take the red commit and the test command from `reviewer.md`, which the engineer agent writes and which the repository's own rules treat as untrusted.

**Description:** Reproduced: the argv after `--` ran as the invoking user with the full environment and filesystem.

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <c> -- bash -c 'echo "I ran as $(id -un) in $PWD with HOME=$HOME"; exit 1'
I ran as node in …/red-test-check.Elibcj/red with HOME=/home/evaluser
I ran as node in …/red-test-check.Elibcj/green with HOME=/home/evaluser
```

The worktree is a scratch cwd, not a sandbox. Confidence is medium rather than high because exploitation needs an attacker-controlled `reviewer.md` or an injected test command; the escalation itself is mechanical.
**Impact:** The narrow allowlist is the fence that keeps the review gate near-read-only and is what makes "the reviewer, not the engineer, runs the check" meaningful. A single `*` grant on an argv runner removes it: `-- bash -c '…'`, `-- git push`, `-- curl … | sh` via a committed script are all permitted, and (MED-001) writes through the linked dependency directories persist in the live tree.
**Remediation:** Replace the wildcard with runner-specific patterns (`Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red * -- bats *)`, `… -- pytest *`, `… -- npm test*`, `… -- go test *`, `… -- cargo test *`) and omit `--setup` from the review grant. In the script, refuse an argv[0] that is a shell or interpreter with an inline-code flag (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, `python -c`, `node -e`) and network fetchers unless `--allow-shell` is given, and print the resolved argv in the verdict. Alternatively read the test command from a committed `Test command:` field in the micro-sprint that the review compares against the diff.
**References:** CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html; CWE-78 OS Command Injection — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html; OWASP ASVS V1.4 Access Control Architecture — https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/. Review Finding 3; review dissent DISS-C-001; audit dissent DISS-C-001 (HIGH). Confirmed by cross-model review and by reproduction.

---

## Medium Priority Issues (Address in Next Sprint)

### [MED-001] Writes through linked dependency directories persist in the live tree

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227`, `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:29` (documented caveat)
**Description:** The red and green commits are engineer-controlled; the symlinks at `:227` give their code write access to the operator's live `node_modules`, `.venv`, `vendor`, `target` and `.tox`. Reproduced: a red-commit test that writes `node_modules/.bin/jest` left the planted file in the live tree after both worktrees were removed. The header documents the behaviour at `:29-30`, but the safe mode is opt-out (`--no-link-deps`) and `SKILL.md:219` does not tell the reviewer to use it.
**Impact:** A hostile or compromised commit plants code that runs on every later tool invocation in the live checkout, long after the review. Compounds HIGH-003.
**Remediation:** Same switch as HIGH-002 (opt-in linking), or copy/hardlink the directories read-only; at minimum have the review skill pass `--no-link-deps` for `/bug` reviews.
**References:** CWE-61 UNIX Symbolic Link (Symlink) Following — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/61.html. Audit dissent DISS-C-002 (MEDIUM). Confirmed by cross-model review and reproduction.

### [MED-002] The test argv inherits the reviewer's full environment and its output is copied into review artifacts

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:248`, `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:250`, `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:144` and `:149` (tails printed)
**Description:** Only `GIT_DIR GIT_WORK_TREE GIT_INDEX_FILE GIT_PREFIX` are unset before `exec`; everything else in the review agent's environment, which in this framework commonly includes provider keys and a GitHub token, reaches the engineer's committed test code. Reproduced: `AUDIT_PROBE_SECRET=sk-test-1234 … -- sh -c 'echo leak=$AUDIT_PROBE_SECRET'` printed the value in both tails, and the tails are what the reviewer is told to cite into `engineer-feedback.md` and what `--json` emits as `red_tail`. Confidence is medium because any test runner inherits its environment; the aggravating factors are the role boundary (HIGH-003) and the artifact copy.
**Impact:** A hostile red commit exfiltrates credentials, or a careless test prints them into tracked review files, which the State Zone rule forbids.

## Changes Required

### [HIGH-001] A test file absent at the red commit yields VERIFIED

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:326` (exit-code gate), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:52` (`NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS`)
**Criterion:** SEC-IV Input Validation / CQ-EH Error Handling

**Reasoning Trace:**
> The red side is accepted as an assertion failure whenever the exit is not 0, 126 or 127 and no pattern matches (`:322-337`). `sh` exits 2 with `cannot open`, `python3` exits 2 with `can't open file … No such file or directory`, `pytest` exits 4 with `file or directory not found`. None of these codes is gated and none of these strings is in the list at `:52-71`. The `--test-file` guard at `:160` would catch it, but both prescribed invocations omit the flag: `head/.claude/skills/bug-triaging/resources/templates/micro-sprint.md:43` and `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:219`.

**Description:** Reproduced in a fixture whose red commit predates the test and whose green commit adds test and fix together, which is exactly the discipline the tool exists to catch:

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <pre-test commit> -- sh tests/test_add.sh
red-test-check: red 4d165e6a… exit 2; green 52f7935d… exit 0; linked deps: none
--- red run (last 80 lines) ---
sh: 0: cannot open tests/test_add.sh: No such file
--- end red run ---
verdict: VERIFIED          (exit 0)
```

**Impact:** The reviewer is told to cite this output as the evidence for "Test fails with current code". A VERIFIED on a red commit that never contained the test is a false attestation of red-before-green, and the micro-sprint's acceptance criterion at `micro-sprint.md:43` is satisfied by exactly the commit shape it forbids.
**Remediation:** (1) Add file-not-found shapes to `NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS`: `cannot open`, `No such file or directory`, `file or directory not found`, `can.t open file`, `ERROR: not found:`. (2) Treat exit 2 from `sh`/`python` and exit 4 from `pytest` as NOT_A_RED when the output names a missing path. (3) Make `--test-file` part of both prescribed invocations, or read it from the micro-sprint's `Test file:` line and refuse to run without it. (4) Add a bats case for the default path with the file absent at red, expecting exit 4 (RTC-3 covers only the `--test-file` path).
**References:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html. Review Finding 1; review dissent DISS-001. Confirmed independently by reproduction.

### [HIGH-002] Linked dependency directories make both runs resolve the live tree's source

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:227` (`ln -s`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:222` (`link_deps`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:27` (the header promise)
**Criterion:** SEC-CI Integrity / ARCH-RE Reliability

**Reasoning Trace:**
> `link_deps` symlinks `node_modules .venv vendor target .tox` from `$MAIN` into each worktree by default (`:47`, `:225-229`). An npm/pnpm/yarn workspace link (`node_modules/pkg -> ../src/pkg`) and an editable Python install (`.pth` naming `$MAIN/src`) both resolve relative to the real directory in the live tree, so a test in the worktree imports the live tree's code, not the checked-out commit's.

**Description:** Reproduced with a shell fixture: `node_modules/pkg -> ../src/pkg` in the live tree, a red commit holding the failing test and the buggy source, a green commit containing no fix, and the fix present only as an uncommitted edit:

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <red> -- sh tests/test_add.sh
red-test-check: the test passes at the red commit: it does not reproduce the bug
red d95711b6… exit 0; green 05e7686c… exit 0; linked deps: node_modules
verdict: DECOY             (exit 3; the green commit contains no fix)
```

Both runs executed the live tree's `src/pkg/lib.sh`. With the buggy source on disk instead, the same mechanism gives a VERIFIED against a green commit that contains no fix. The header at `:27` states "Uncommitted state in the live tree never counts"; the caveat at `:29-30` covers writes, not source resolution.
**Impact:** Wrong verdicts in the tool's core job for the two ecosystems the dependency list targets first. A legitimate pair is blocked as DECOY whenever the operator has the fix checked out; an uncommitted fix can mint a VERIFIED the reviewer is told to cite.
**Remediation:** Make linking opt-in (`--link-deps`) with a WARN naming the directories, or refuse to link a directory that resolves back into `$MAIN`: for `.venv`/`.tox` scan `site-packages` for `*.pth` and `__editable__*` entries that reference `$MAIN`; for `node_modules` refuse when any top-level or scoped entry is a symlink resolving outside `node_modules`. Point the help text at `--setup` for per-worktree installs. Add a bats case with a workspace-style link that expects NOT_A_RED or a refusal, never DECOY. Amend `:27` to state the remaining caveat.
**References:** CWE-706 Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/706.html. Review Finding 2; review dissent DISS-C-002. Confirmed independently by reproduction.

### [HIGH-003] The review role's allowlist now contains a universal exec wrapper

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:6` (`allowed-tools`), `head/.claude/skills/reviewing-code/SKILL.md:27` (`args: ["*"]`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:250` (`exec "$@"`), `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:113` (`--setup` argv)
**Criterion:** SEC-AZ Authorization

**Reasoning Trace:**
> The review skill declares `deny_raw_shell: true` (`:39`) and allowlists `git diff`, `git log` and a fixed set of scripts. The change adds `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)`. The script validates `--red`, `--green`, `--timeout` and `--test-file` and then execs everything after `--` verbatim (`:248`, `:250`), plus a second arbitrary argv from `--setup` (`:113`, `:292`). Phase 2 at `SKILL.md:219` instructs the reviewer to take the red commit and the test command from `reviewer.md`, which the engineer agent writes and which the repository's own rules treat as untrusted.

**Description:** Reproduced: the argv after `--` ran as the invoking user with the full environment and filesystem.

```
$ red-test-check.sh --red <c> -- bash -c 'echo "I ran as $(id -un) in $PWD with HOME=$HOME"; exit 1'
I ran as node in …/red-test-check.Elibcj/red with HOME=/home/evaluser
I ran as node in …/red-test-check.Elibcj/green with HOME=/home/evaluser
```

The worktree is a scratch cwd, not a sandbox. Confidence is medium rather than high because exploitation needs an attacker-controlled `reviewer.md` or an injected test command; the escalation itself is mechanical.
**Impact:** The narrow allowlist is the fence that keeps the review gate near-read-only and is what makes "the reviewer, not the engineer, runs the check" meaningful. A single `*` grant on an argv runner removes it: `-- bash -c '…'`, `-- git push`, `-- curl … | sh` via a committed script are all permitted, and (MED-001) writes through the linked dependency directories persist in the live tree.
**Remediation:** Replace the wildcard with runner-specific patterns (`Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red * -- bats *)`, `… -- pytest *`, `… -- npm test*`, `… -- go test *`, `… -- cargo test *`) and omit `--setup` from the review grant. In the script, refuse an argv[0] that is a shell or interpreter with an inline-code flag (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, `python -c`, `node -e`) and network fetchers unless `--allow-shell` is given, and print the resolved argv in the verdict. Alternatively read the test command from a committed `Test command:` field in the micro-sprint that the review compares against the diff.
**References:** CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html; CWE-78 OS Command Injection — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html; OWASP ASVS V1.4 Access Control Architecture — https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/. Review Finding 3; review dissent DISS-C-001; audit dissent DISS-C-001 (HIGH). Confirmed by cross-model review and by reproduction.

### [MED-003] The fallback timeout never reaches its KILL step

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh:275`, `:260` (the 2 s sleep), `:270` (`wait "$RUN_PID"`)
**Description:** Without `timeout`/`gtimeout`, the watcher sends TERM to the process group and sleeps two seconds before KILL, but `wait "$RUN_PID"` returns as soon as the direct child dies, `RUN_PID` is cleared at `:273`, and the watcher is killed at `:275` mid-sleep. A grandchild that ignores TERM survives the run and the cleanup (which only signals a non-empty `RUN_PID`). The review reproduced two orphaned `sleep 300` processes with a TERM-ignoring child; confirmed here by code reading. RTC-8 and RTC-9 use `sleep`, which honours TERM, so they cannot see it.
**Impact:** Orphaned test processes holding ports or writing through linked dependency directories after a TIMEOUT on macOS without coreutils.
**Remediation:** When the timed-out flag is set, `wait "$WATCH_PID"` instead of killing it so the KILL lands; in `cleanup` signal the recorded process group rather than relying on `RUN_PID`; add a TERM-ignoring child to RTC-9.
**References:** CWE-404 Improper Resource Shutdown or Release — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/404.html. Review Observation 2; review dissent DISS-002.
